name: Extreme heat
value: Cape York warning to 19 Nov; Philippine heat
summary: Queensland's severe heatwave warning ran to 19 Nov; PAGASA forecast danger-level heat indices; no deadly heatwave found
state: The Bureau of Meteorology's severe heatwave warning for Far North Queensland ran to 19 Nov, after Weipa logged 41 straight days above 36°C, its longest run on record (The Watchers). PAGASA forecast danger-level heat indices of 42–44°C at eight Philippine stations on 18 Nov (GMA News), and Brazil's Inmet reported highs near 40°C in the Centre-West and North on 13–16 Nov (Latin Times). Searches on 20 Nov found no deadly heatwave under top-tier warnings; Watch is kept while warnings ease, with a fall to Normal likely if no new warnings follow.
for_you: Older people, young children and outdoor workers in northern Australia, the Philippines and central Brazil are most exposed. Follow national weather service and health ministry heat advice.
rubric_hit: Watch: regional severe heatwave warning (Far North Queensland, to 19 Nov); no top-tier deadly heatwave for Alert

why: Heat is the deadliest weather hazard globally, straining power grids, crops and health systems.
drivers: Heat domes, climate warming, season, humidity, urban heat islands.

rubric.alert: Deadly heatwave with top-tier official warnings across a large population.
rubric.watch: Heatwave warnings across a major region, or national temperature records.
rubric.normal: No major heatwaves affecting large populations.
